purpose: Machine-readable chronology of major IsoGraph and Project Discovery ideas, formulations, mission changes, and contribution boundaries. Entries state earliest evidence currently located; they are not global priority determinations.

entries.title: Agent-oriented compact reasoning representation / context-logic incubation

conversation_evidence.summary: Stated that the language was for agents, emphasizing context-window compactness and synthesis of concepts.

reasoning_path: Complex reasoning can exceed available context/working-state capacity even when local operations are tractable.
A compact state should preserve propositions, dependencies, scopes, alternatives, provenance, and inference obligations.
History may be quotiented only when valid future continuations remain unchanged.
The first public Axiomesh record therefore framed a search for a token-efficient, recoverable logical/structural state for agents.
entries.notes: The seed README explicitly says 'Research direction: Josh Oshiro'. 'Josh Oshiro' is the historical short-form name for Joshua Oshiro.

entries.title: Graph/hypergraph rewrite substrate and structure-plus-transformation formulation

attribution.detail: Adopted the proposal as a candidate research direction and continued directing its development.

earliest_evidence.summary: Assistant proposed graph/hypergraph rewriting as a candidate substrate and the formulation of knowledge as structure plus lawful transformation.

reasoning_path: The initial Markov-like sufficient-state idea had to preserve nonlocal dependencies, guards, quantifiers, alternatives, and provenance.
The design pressure favored a sparse typed relational structure over a simple chain.
Graph/hypergraph rewriting unified represented state and lawful transformation while supporting composition, self-representation, isomorphism, and residual accounting.
entries.notes: This record deliberately does not attribute the graph/hypergraph-rewrite proposal or the compact structure-plus-transformation wording solely to Joshua Oshiro.

entries.title: One semantic structure / no mandatory internal translation boundary
reasoning_path: A translator between a source formalism and a separate agent formalism would confound representation, decomposition, mapping, and translation loss.
The project therefore made the structural form both semantic representation and native wire representation, with human/theorem-prover/database views downstream.
entries.notes: The surviving evidence establishes the design under Joshua's research direction but does not support clean sole-origin attribution for this exact formulation.

entries.title: IsoGraph name and standalone migration from Axiomesh/AxiomeSH

attribution.detail: The assistant surfaced the IsoGraph naming option; Joshua explicitly selected/accepted it.

conversation_evidence.summary: Explicitly accepted the IsoGraph name ('Isograph is cool too') during the rename discussion.

public_evidence.description: Standalone migration of the AxiomeSH corpus.
Completed IsoGraph naming migration without semantic change.

entries.title: Observation-first discrepancy handling: error/defect may be a clue

conversation_evidence.summary: Stated that a discrepancy might be a clue to look deeper rather than something to normalize away immediately.
Accepted and reinforced an observation-first posture: anomalies should be understood before judging or repairing them.
Strengthened the rule: discrepancies/errors should be preserved and investigated as possible clues; even the expected/reference authority may be wrong.
Clarified that concrete examples normally express a general principle, not a request for a special-case rule.

reasoning_path: Unexpected mismatch may indicate a bug, hidden distinction, hidden equivalence, wrong reference expectation, scope mismatch, or unresolved structure.
Therefore preserve the observation before assigning defect ownership.
When repair is justified, use it as a diagnostic intervention and see what disappears or survives.
Keep repair disposition separate from discovery disposition.

entries.title: Project Discovery named cross-domain discovery campaigns

attribution.party: Joshua Oshiro + agent-assisted IsoGraph research process

artifact_evidence.title: Project Discovery — Ising / MWC DP 0.7 Campaign

entries.notes: The campaign file is self-dated September 25; the located main-branch preservation commit is September 26. The current audit does not claim that the self-date is independently public timestamp evidence.

entries.title: Corpus-wide Project Discovery vision

earliest_evidence.summary: Proposed rendering mathematics, physics, computational/complexity-theory and related papers into IsoGraph, then running Discovery Protocol across the corpus to find cross-domain isomorphs and discoveries.

agent_contribution.summary: Expanded the proposal into corpus-wide structural discovery with common cores/residuals, candidate isomorphs/generalizations, structural indexing, falsification, and validation.

reasoning_path: Individual structural renderings had already shown value for exposing non-obvious relationships.
A corpus of exact renderings would permit retrieval/comparison beyond one hand-selected pair.
Discovery Protocol could then search within and across disciplines while residual accounting limits false equivalence.

entries.title: Primitive-logic / no-high-level-authoritative-leaf doctrine

conversation_evidence.summary: Required IsoGraph to reduce structure to irreducible, invariant primitives; high-level abstractions belong in discovery/derived views rather than the authoritative Core.
Reiterated that everything authoritative must reduce to irreducible logic and only fundamental logical properties may remain at the bottom.

reasoning_path: High-level names can conceal exactly the structure needed for discovery.
A source-faithful representation may retain convenient labels only as derived/reconstructible views.
Definitionally reducible semantics should not remain opaque authoritative leaves.

entries.title: Implicit Assertions and recursive fixed-point passes

attribution.detail: Explicitly required careful recursive passes and later IA/NEI alternation until a scoped fixed point.

conversation_evidence.summary: Directed that implicit assertions be filled carefully and recursively because missing one could miss the opportunity to solve the problem.
Directed a scoped loop: Core first, then implicit assertions, then NEI, then implicit assertions again, repeating until finished within scope.

entries.notes: The current evidence establishes IA publicly before the later explicit Joshua fixed-point directives; it does not support sole attribution of the original IA concept to one participant.

entries.title: Minimum Sufficient Support / Valuation

attribution.detail: Supplied broader pressure toward the shortest/laziest exact route and approved/pursued the successor research.

precursor_conversation.summary: Asked for the 'laziest path' / shortest exact route to the same conclusion without changing inputs or the solution.

entries.notes: The specific DP 0.9 MSS/Valuation formalization is not claimed as solely Joshua-originated. The surviving record supports a broader Joshua optimization principle followed by agent formalization into the module.

entries.title: Experimental Warrant and open-world Experimental Inquiry

attribution.detail: Required clues to trigger experimentation and required experiments to operate over incomplete working models rather than falsely complete models.

conversation_evidence.summary: Required clues to trigger experimentation and to inform intervention scope rather than prematurely narrowing the experiment.
Required experiments to work from incomplete 'Lego' models with possibly unknown pieces, outputs, dimensions, and completeness.

entries.title: No-Evasion, Source Semantic Census, Schema Closure, and IA invalidation

attribution.detail: Repeatedly required complete primitive reduction and forbade evading hard-to-reduce semantics or shrinking scope.
Formalized the pressure into SSC conservation, closure dispositions, Schema Closure, and machine-derived ledger controls.

conceptual_precursors.summary: Joshua reiterated that high-level abstractions cannot terminate authoritative reduction.
Joshua required integration under updated standards, recursive IA until none remain, and no evasion of hard-to-reduce semantics.

entries.notes: The exact terms Source Semantic Census and Schema Closure, and the hardened ledger machinery, are recorded as agent-assisted formalization rather than retrospectively assigned as Joshua's original wording.

entries.title: Grand-scale Project Discovery mission: mass research synthesis with hundreds/thousands of agents

conversation_evidence.summary: Described current Project Discovery as a small proof/example collection and the intended mature system as mass research synthesis across and within domains, potentially using hundreds or thousands of agents and much greater server resources.
Clarified that full realization would require substantial funding, people, talent, and help because one person could not manage that scale alone.

agent_formalization.summary: Assistant characterized the present work as a prototype/validation environment and the mature target as a massively parallel, continuously compounding structural research-synthesis system.

entries.title: Publication authorship and agent-assistance attribution rule

conversation_evidence.summary: Required Joshua Oshiro authorship, IsoGraph Project attribution, disclosure of agent assistance, and explicit statement that IsoGraph was designed by Joshua Oshiro.

entries.title: External parallel-work awareness and provenance audit trigger
entries.summary: After identifying substantial philosophical and research-direction overlap with active work at the Wolfram Institute, Joshua directed a comprehensive provenance audit so IsoGraph and Project Discovery ideas/findings would preserve origin, reasoning path, authorship/contribution, and dated evidence.

external_trigger.note: The URL is preserved as the trigger supplied by Joshua. This ledger does not infer priority or copying from the video.

external_antecedent_boundary.note: The Institute states it was initially launched in October 2022 and pursues computational foundational science.

external_antecedent_boundary.source: Stephen Wolfram, Can AI Solve Science?
external_antecedent_boundary.note: Public prior discussion of AI/computation in scientific discovery. This is one reason Project Discovery provenance claims must be architecture-specific rather than generic AI-for-science priority claims.

entries.title: Woit-Lisi IsoGraph structural comparison campaign

earliest_evidence.summary: Joshua identified Peter Woit's and Garrett Lisi's programs as candidates for an IsoGraph isomorph search and directed that the work receive its own research directory.

entries.title: Mandatory intra-author formulation-family recovery before cross-domain bridge selection

earliest_evidence.summary: Joshua observed that Woit and Lisi often use multiple formulations of the same ideas, not all equally translatable, and directed the campaign to identify same-author alternative expressions and determine which representatives bridge most strongly in each direction.

reasoning_path: A one-rendering-per-author comparison can create false negatives when the chosen representatives expose different structure.
It can also create false positives if a convenient representative cannot be transported back through the author's other formulations.
Therefore recover same-author formulation families blindly before cross-domain comparison.
Treat representative preference as bridge-objective-relative and evidence-bounded rather than as a globally canonical formulation.

public_formalization.note: Formalized in the same work cycle as this provenance entry.

entries.title: Full independent IsoGraph treatment of both Woit and Lisi programs before cross-domain comparison

earliest_evidence.summary: Joshua directed that both theories receive the full IsoGraph treatment, not merely bridge-sufficient partial renderings.

consequence: Each author becomes an independent full-treatment research track.
Full SSC, primitive closure, recursive IA, NEI, DTS, DP, reconstruction, and sealing are required independently.
Cross-author comparison becomes downstream of the two sealed treatments.

public_formalization.note: Formalized in the same work cycle.

entries.title: Isomorph-exposure frontier for axiomatic abstraction

earliest_evidence.summary: Joshua identified the abstraction boundary as a discovery variable: abstract far enough to expose likely isomorphic generative structures, but not so far that load-bearing distinctions are erased.

reasoning_path: The source mathematical objects are too large for extensional IsoGraph representation.
An axiomatic representation is therefore required.
Too-concrete axioms hide cross-formulation structure; too-abstract axioms create trivial false correspondences.
Use nested source-preserving abstractions and stop at the deepest nontrivial common quotient that still reconstructs the relevant source views.

entries.title: Quaternionic chiral-action / projective-twistor incidence representation-transform candidate

attribution.detail: Explicitly identifies the quaternionic vector/chiral-spinor relation as Euclidean twistor incidence and cites Woit 2021.
Provides the Euclidean quaternionic/projective twistor geometry and twistor-P1 formulation.
Identified the B01-to-B02 representation transform as the strongest current bridge candidate under the formulation-family/isomorph-exposure method.

entries.supported_scope: Strong provisional bridge candidate only; no cross-track isomorphism admitted before full-track sealing.
cautions: External sources predate the IsoGraph campaign; no novelty claim is made for the mathematical relation.
Projective well-definedness, source-local type/reality/chirality conditions, reconstruction, and residual accounting remain to be proved in the native treatments.

entries.title: Graph-projectivization as the current Woit-Lisi bridge invariant

attribution.detail: The graph of a linear map is a subspace and can be projectivized.
Supplies vectors as Hom(S_R,S_L), two-plane twistor geometry, and CP3/CP1 Euclidean projective structure.
Supplies vector/chiral-spinor multiplication and identifies the quaternionic case with Euclidean twistor incidence.
Isolated the typed-action -> graph -> projective-incidence transform as the strongest current neutral common quotient.

entries.supported_scope: Pre-seal common-core candidate. Native source instantiation, NEI, residual reconstruction, and post-seal comparison remain outstanding.

entries.title: Paired complex-structure intertwiner as the convention-safe BT01 frontier

attribution.detail: Separates Euclidean vectors, complexified Hom(S_R,S_L), and quaternionic/pseudoreal twistor structure.
Provides real quaternionic chiral multiplication plus a Pauli-matrix complex representation.
Rejected an overly strong common scalar convention and isolated A_v J_minus = J_plus A_v as the safer common invariant.

cautions: Exact source-local J_minus/J_plus identifications and handedness remain open.

entries.title: Unit-octonion lower common quotient with asymmetric theory role

attribution.detail: Explicitly identifies S7 with unit octonions in speculative generation/open-problem discussion.
Develops octonion composition, Clifford, so(8), and triality structure.
Separated the shared unit-composition quotient from stronger triality/generation claims and preserved evidence-state asymmetry.

entries.title: Quaternionic complex-structure choice fiber as a bridge generator

attribution.detail: Unit imaginary quaternions parameterize a sphere of compatible complex structures; Woit explicitly presents the twistor CP1 this way.
Identified the complex-structure choice family as the missing transport parameter between Lisi's real quaternionic chiral relation and the complex projective BT01 presentation.

cautions: Left/right multiplication and chirality/orientation components remain unresolved.

entries.title: Quaternionic anti-involution connects left/right B06 complex-structure families

attribution.detail: Explicitly states multiplication-order reversal under division-algebra conjugation.
Used the anti-involution identity to remove the purely algebraic left/right obstruction while preserving source-role uncertainty.

entries.title: Exact affine HP1 source-formula witness

attribution.detail: Provides affine HP1 coordinates (s,Zs), infinity, and CP3->HP1 fibration.
Provides the division spinor pair (psi,tilde(chi)) with tilde(chi)=v psi.
Observed the exact scoped formula alignment Z=v, s=psi, Zs=tilde(chi) independently of the cross-reference.

cautions: Scoped to finite H chart; global HP1 compactification remains Woit residual.
No cross-track NEI SAME or theory equivalence is claimed.

entries.title: Shift from Woit-Lisi bridge discovery to constructive unification synthesis

earliest_evidence.summary: Joshua stated that the target of the project had shifted from finding a bridge to unifying the two programs.

consequence: The frozen BT01 common structure becomes an input kernel rather than the research endpoint.
A project-generated unification workbench is created, separate from the two source-authority tracks.
The synthesis is optimized for conservative reconstruction and minimal new axioms.
Formal unification promotion remains blocked until the two independent source tracks seal and post-seal validation is complete.
